state.paragraph: On June 24, 2013, the Mac-Gray Board of Directors held a regularly scheduled meeting. By invitation of the Board, certain members of management, including Mr. MacDonald, Mr. Shea, Mr. MacLellan, Mr. Emma, Ms. Serafini and Sheff Halsey, our chief marketing officer and an executive vice president, and representatives from Goodwin Procter were also present for some or all of the meeting. During this meeting, representatives of Goodwin Procter reviewed for the Board its fiduciary duties in the context of considering strategic alternatives that might be available to Mac-Gray, including a potential sale of the company. The Board also discussed, with input from the members of the Transaction Committee, whether it would be appropriate for each of Mr. MacDonald and Mr. Rothenberg to be excluded from the Board's consideration of strategic alternatives in view of the possibility that Mr. MacDonald and/or Moab could be asked to partner with a potential acquiror given their respective equity stakes in Mac-Gray. Following this discussion, the Board decided, and Mr. MacDonald and Mr. Rothenberg agreed, that it would be appropriate to exclude Mr. MacDonald and Mr. Rothenberg from the Board's evaluation of strategic alternatives and any negotiations with third parties that might take place. Mr. MacDonald excused himself after such discussion. In furtherance of the conclusion to exclude Mr. MacDonald and Mr. Rothenberg from the Board's evaluation of strategic alternatives, the Board then established the Special Committee, comprised of the six independent and disinterested members of the Board (namely, Mr. Bullock, Mr. Daoust, Mr. Hyman, William F. Meagher, Bruce A. Percelay and Alastair G. Robinson), to, among other things, explore strategic alternatives to enhance value to Mac-Gray's stockholders and to recommend to the Board the advisability of any such strategic alternative. In connection with this delegation of authority, the Special Committee was further authorized to (a) consider and evaluate all proposals that might be received by Mac-Gray in connection with a possible sale or other significant business transaction, through any form of transaction, including, without limitation, merger, stock purchase, asset purchase, recapitalization, reorganization, going-private transaction, consolidation, amalgamation or other transaction, (b) participate in and direct the negotiation of the material terms and conditions of any such transaction, (c) consider any alternatives to any such transaction, including without limitation, Mac-Gray's continuing to operate as an independent company and (d) recommend to the Board the advisability of entering into a definitive agreement with respect to any such transaction. Mr. Bullock was appointed chairman of the Special Committee. It was also determined that the Transaction Committee would function as a sub-committee of the Special Committee for the purpose of taking any administrative actions to discharge the duties and responsibilities of the Special Committee.

ledger_rows.Note: Re-engaged as the target's sole financial adviser for the strategic review and possible sale, chosen from three banks. Engagement letter 05/31; no buyer financing without consent.
Moab (about 9% holder) won a proxy contest; Rothenberg and Hyman replaced incumbents. The filing does not say Moab pressed for a sale. Rothenberg was later excluded over Moab's rollover interest.
Unsolicited proposal to the board, made before any NDA or diligence (Heavy by context). It was still standing when round 1 was evaluated on 07/25.
Board forms a Special Committee of six independent directors, excluding CEO MacDonald and Moab's Rothenberg. The committee will weigh a sale against staying stand-alone and approach 50 parties.
BofA's outreach carries out the 06/24 decision; contacts reported by 06/28. NDA signers get an informational package, with preliminary IOIs due 07/23/2013 (no separate Deadline set row).

ledger_rows.When: during the next several weeks after 06/24/2013
ledger_rows.Note: Target outreach. Of 50 contacted (15 strategic, 35 financial), Party A (#2) and CSC/Pamplona (#10) are recorded separately, leaving 13 strategic parties.

ledger_rows.When: during the next several weeks after 06/24/2013
ledger_rows.Note: Target outreach to all 35 financial parties (including private equity), among them Party B and Party C. 50 contacted in total.

ledger_rows.When: over the two months after late June 2013
ledger_rows.Note: 20 NDAs in total (2 strategic, 18 financial). Party A, CSC/Pamplona, Party B and Party C have their own rows, leaving 16 financial. Signing dates not given; each got an informational package.
Due date for preliminary IOIs. CSC/Pamplona bid on time; Party B and Party C bid on 07/24 and were considered on 07/25 (late bids accepted).

adviser.instructions: `paragraph` reports that a financial or legal adviser is retained, engaged, terminated or first shown acting for the target, a committee or a bidder. Is every such event in `paragraph` recorded by some entry in `ledger_rows` (same party, same kind of event, consistent date)?

criteria.true: Each such event has a matching ledger entry, possibly summarised in an entry's Note.
criteria.false: At least one such event in the paragraph has no matching ledger entry.
